episodes.180270: Scattered thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee on July 2, 2023. With favorable instability and wind shear, some of these thunderstorms turned strong to severe over the area. Damaging winds were again the main threat with reports received of trees down, but one thunderstorm over Smyrna did produce half-dollar size hail.
episodes.180271: On the afternoon of the second, scattered thunderstorms developed within a low level upslope flow area in eastern New Mexico. These storms persisted into the South Plains of West Texas on a strong cold pool. Outflow winds just ahead of the thunderstorms produced severe wind gusts near Anton (Hockley County).
episodes.180274: An isolated sub-severe thunderstorm developed in Aiken Co SC in the early morning hours.
episodes.180304: A mesoscale vorticity maximum triggered thunderstorms in the eastern Carolinas.
episodes.180318: Isolated to scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the early to mid afternoon hours.
episodes.180695: A broad positively tilted upper trough continued to extend from the Great Lakes Region and Mid-Mississippi Valley southwest into North Texas during the afternoon of July 3rd, while an associated weak surface front lifted back north before becoming stationary across Southeast Oklahoma and Western/Central Arkansas. Strong heating within a moist air mass resulted in strong instability developing during the afternoon, with large scale forcing ahead of the trough adequate enough for the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms across portions of Southeast Oklahoma, Southwest Arkansas, Northeast Texas, and Northwest Louisiana during the afternoon. One isolated severe thunderstorm developed over Downtown Shreveport, and produced a 58 mph wind gust at the Shreveport Downtown Airport.
episodes.180696: A broad positively tilted upper trough continued to extend from the Great Lakes Region and Mid-Mississippi Valley southwest into North Texas during the afternoon of July 3rd, while an associated weak surface front lifted back north before becoming stationary across Southeast Oklahoma and Western/Central Arkansas. Strong heating within a moist air mass resulted in strong instability developing during the afternoon, with large scale forcing ahead of the trough adequate enough for the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms across portions of Southeast Oklahoma, Southwest Arkansas, Northeast Texas, and Northwest Louisiana during the afternoon. One isolated severe thunderstorm developed over Eastern Cass County Texas, with damaging winds downing a tree just southeast of Atlanta.
episodes.180697: A broad positively tilted upper trough continued to extend from the Great Lakes Region and Mid-Mississippi Valley southwest into North Texas during the afternoon of July 3rd, while an associated weak surface front lifted back north before becoming stationary across Southeast Oklahoma and Western/Central Arkansas. Strong heating within a moist air mass resulted in strong instability developing during the afternoon, with large scale forcing ahead of the trough adequate enough for the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms across portions of Southeast Oklahoma, Southwest Arkansas, Northeast Texas, and Northwest Louisiana during the afternoon. One isolated severe thunderstorm developed over Northeast McCurtain County Oklahoma, producing damaging winds which downed multiple trees near Smithville. Large hail was also observed from this storm.
episodes.180719: Following scattered convection throughout the afternoon hours, a more cohesive squall line formed over Utah's West Desert region. This squall progressed eastward through the northern portions of the state, resulting in a swath of strong to very strong wind gusts, due in part to low dew points and dry low levels of the atmosphere.
episodes.180806: Thunderstorms with strong outflow winds developed across Carbon County during the afternoon of the 3rd continuing northeast into east-central Wyoming through the evening.
episodes.181194: A weak disturbance moved over West Virginia on July 2nd, bringing a broken line of showers and thunderstorms through early in the day. Additional activity sprouted up ahead of and along a cold front later that evening. Severe storms developed during the second round of activity, resulting in many downed trees across the state.
episodes.181276: A severe thunderstorm developed over the Piedmont area and moved southeastward into the Rapid City area. Hail around golf ball size was reported across these areas.
episodes.181279: A severe thunderstorm quickly developed over the northern Black Hills and moved south-southeast into portions of the central Black Hills. The storm produced large hail to golf ball size.
episodes.181281: A severe thunderstorm developed quickly across far southern portions of Rapid City and tracked south-southeast across the eastern foothills and adjacent plains. The storm produced hail as large as baseballs east of Rockerville. As the storm weakened, wind gusts to 60 mph developed over the plains.
episodes.181399: A stationary front across Central New York and a passing weak disturbance supported scattered thunderstorms. One storm became severe with damaging wind gusts. One motorist was injured when a tree fell on their car.
episodes.181582: An advancing cold front along the Ohio and Tennessee valleys combined with a Piedmont trough over western North Carolina and a very moist atmosphere to produce widely isolated to scattered thunderstorms. A swath of severe thunderstorms developed over the northern Coastal Plain in Halifax County, producing damaging straight-line winds and downed trees.
episodes.181598: A slow moving front and a very moist airmass yielded slow moving thunderstorms that dumped heavy rain over southeast Wyoming county with portions of park roads and hiking trails flooded at Letchworth State Park. The front then stalled out during the evening along the New York and Pennsylvania state line leading to multiple rounds of slow moving thunderstorms crossing the same areas with drenching rains. Significant flash flooding occurred over southwest Allegany county in Bolivar and Richburg, where some roads were washed out. Some of these road closures may last for a while.
episodes.181689: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed within the vicinity of a stationary frontal boundary during the afternoon and early evening hours on July 3, 2023. One thunderstorm downed a tree onto cars at an apartment complex in East Greenbush.
episodes.181692: A strong upper-level ridge extended over the region. Light steering flow enabled sea breezes to develop and move inland into the afternoon with a few to isolated strong pulse severe storms along boundary mergers over a very moist and unstable airmass. Local heat advisories were in effect for heat index values 108-112 degrees. A high rip current risk continued at local beaches.
episodes.181696: High moisture and SW steering flow fueled scattered strong to pulse severe storms along boundary mergers during the afternoon and early evening.  PWAT was near 2 inches.
episodes.181697: High moisture and SW steering flow fueled scattered strong to pulse severe storms along boundary mergers during the afternoon and early evening. PWAT was near 2 inches.
episodes.181861: A couple of severe thunderstorms initiated off the bay breeze near and to the south of Baltimore. Meanwhile, a couple of isolated thunderstorms produced sporadic wind damage further west in the vicinity of a lee pressure trough.
episodes.181864: A couple of severe thunderstorms initiated off the bay breeze near and to the south of Baltimore. Meanwhile, a couple of isolated thunderstorms produced sporadic wind damage further west in the vicinity of a lee pressure trough.
episodes.181865: A cold front sparked a few lines of thunderstorms. These thunderstorms produced localized wind damage, most notably over northeastern Maryland during the early evening hours.
episodes.181866: A cold front sparked a few lines of thunderstorms. These thunderstorms produced localized wind damage, most notably over northeastern Maryland during the early evening hours.
episodes.181935: A couple of thunderstorms initiated off the bay breeze near and to the south of Baltimore.
episodes.181936: A cold front sparked a few lines of thunderstorms. These thunderstorms produced localized gale- to storm-force winds.
episodes.181967: A cold front passed through the region producing damaging thunderstorm winds across the Virginia Southside. Shear and high instability aided in the development and strength of these thunderstorms.
episodes.182055: A cold front passed through the region producing damaging thunderstorm winds across the southeast West Virginia. Shear and high instability aided in the development and strength of these thunderstorms.
episodes.182107: A cold front moved eastward from the Ohio Valley during the afternoon of July 3, 2023, which led to an organized line of thunderstorms advancing into the region. Abundant moisture an very warm temperatures created an environment that supported strong downdraft winds from thunderstorms. As the increased moisture converged along the higher terrain of the mountains, scattered thunderstorms developed, and caused pockets of wind damage.
episodes.182162: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed in the vicinity of a weak cold/surface front across central into southern Oklahoma on the afternoon of the 3rd. Despite weak magnitudes of organizing wind shear, a few storms produced reports of large hail and damaging wind across the aforementioned areas.
episodes.182248: The first of many rounds of rain moved into the state by daybreak on July 2nd.  Periods of moderate to heavy rain continued through most of the day before ending by evening.  Most areas of the state received 1 to 2��� of rain, with the heaviest rain corridor occurring across the Seacoast region of Rockingham and Strafford Counties where 2 to 3������ of rainfall occurred.
episodes.182335: Showers and thunderstorms developed across the Ohio Valley as a low pressure system moved through the region.
episodes.182616: An area of low pressure over northern Manitoba trailed a cold front across the Northland on July 3rd. Storms developed ahead of the front during the afternoon and evening hours with storms becoming strong to severe across northwest Wisconsin. These storms took on a linear mode with an associated damaging wind threat as they moved across the region. These damaging winds led to reports of downed trees and powerlines as they progressed to the east.
episodes.182673: Showers and thunderstorms developed in a very warm and moist airmass as a disturbance moved through. Storms produced damaging wind gusts across parts of eastern Pennsylvania.
episodes.182674: Showers and thunderstorms developed in a very warm and moist airmass as a disturbance moved through. Storms produced damaging wind gusts across parts of northern Delaware.
episodes.182675: Showers and thunderstorms developed in a very warm and moist airmass as a disturbance moved through. Storms produced damaging wind gusts across parts of the Eastern Shore of Maryland.
episodes.182678: A cold front approached the region, with scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developing out ahead of it, producing damaging wind gusts across parts of Delaware.
episodes.182679: A cold front approached the region, with scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developing out ahead of it, producing damaging wind gusts across parts of Maryland.
episodes.182785: An isolated thunderstorm produced some quarter size hail.
episodes.182895: A trough across the southern Rocky Mountains helped develop afternoon strong to severe thunderstorms across the higher elevations and adjacent plains. Isolated severe wind gusts were reported.
episodes.182980: Thunderstorms moved through Eastern NC during the afternoon hours, several of which became severe and produced damaging straight-line winds of 70 to 90 mph.
episodes.183001: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
episodes.183059: During the afternoon of the 2nd a convective complex formed over portions of northeast NM and far western OK Panhandle. This complex moved southeast through much of the western and central portions of the Texas Panhandle. While doing so the storm system bowed out and produced widespread wind gusts ranging from 58 to 65 mph.
episodes.183084: A cold front moved eastward from the Ohio Valley during the afternoon of July 3, 2023, which led to an organized line of thunderstorms advancing into southeast West Virginia. As the increased moisture converged along the higher terrain of the mountains, scattered thunderstorms developed, and caused a several trees to be blown down in Mercer County.
episodes.183126: Thunderstorms moved across an unstable airmass located mostly over Mississippi, Alabama, and Western Georgia in the afternoon hours. Storms were able to produce outflow strong enough to further develop spotty clustering of thunderstorms across North and Northeast GA.
episodes.183277: A weak upper level trough remained stagnant over North and Central Texas during the first week of July, generating isolated thunderstorms each afternoon. A few storms produced marginally severe hail and wind damage on the 3rd and 4th of July, while one slow-moving storm cluster produced flash flooding in Denton County.
episodes.183292: A weak cold front pushed toward the Mid-South during the afternoon and evening of July 2, 2023. A very unstable airmass was in place across the region and isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms developed as temperatures warmed into the 90s. A mid-level trough moving north of the region provided enough wind shear for storm organization. As a result, some storms became severe with large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.183344: In early July there were significant reports of hail, damaging wind, and flash flooding. The month got off to a quick start with golf ball size hail just east of Omaha (Boone County) on the 1st. On the 5th, there was a 62 mph wind gust measured at Newport (Jackson County).
episodes.183350: Rainfall during the previous day, plus during the morning of July 2nd, kept the ground saturated. An early afternoon break in rainfall was followed by additional thunderstorm development in western and central Ohio by late afternoon.  These storms took advantage of an environment containing 1500 J/kg of surface-based CAPE, along with marginal sufficient deep shear of 30 knots to create severe thunderstorms with a number of wind damage reports in Ohio.  Southwest Pennsylvania only saw isolated flash flooding in Allegheny County from this event.
episodes.183351: Rainfall during the previous day, plus during the morning of July 2nd, kept the ground saturated. An early afternoon break in rainfall was followed by additional thunderstorm development in western and central Ohio by late afternoon.  These storms took advantage of an environment containing 1500 J/kg of surface-based CAPE, along with marginal sufficient deep shear of 30 knots to create severe thunderstorms with a number of wind damage reports.  Isolated flash flooding was also reported in Tuscarawas County with repeated rounds of heavy rain.
episodes.183352: Rainfall during the previous day, plus during the morning of July 2nd, kept the ground saturated. An early afternoon break in rainfall was followed by additional thunderstorm development in western and central Ohio by late afternoon.  These storms took advantage of an environment containing 1500 J/kg of surface-based CAPE, along with marginal sufficient deep shear of 30 knots to create severe thunderstorms with a number of wind damage reports in Ohio.  Only single reports of wind damage and flash flooding were received from Hancock County in West Virginia.
episodes.183374: Weak warm advection continued to push across Iowa beneath thermal ridging, especially towards northwest Iowa into Minnesota. By evening convection had developed along this gradient. While much of this remained sub-severe and confined to Minnesota, a few isolated storms did develop in northwest Iowa with one resulting in quarter sized hail.
episodes.183423: A stationary front draped over the region provided the focus for slow moving thunderstorm activity over northeastern Pennsylvania. Localized areas of 2 to 4 inches of rainfall contributed to some small stream and creek flooding near the Delaware River.
episodes.183443: A slow moving front and shortwave trough aloft approached from the west. A cluster of thunderstorms developed over eastern Pennsylvania and moved east over the waters. One of the thunderstorms was able to produce a severe wind gust.
episodes.183448: Isolated severe thunderstorm associated with a weak surface trough produced damaging winds across portions of central Virginia.
episodes.183449: Scattered severe thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds across portions of central, eastern and southeast Virginia.
episodes.183450: Scattered severe thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds, lightning damage and one tornado across portions of northeast North Carolina.
episodes.183453: Scattered severe thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds across portions of the Lower Maryland Eastern Shore.
episodes.183480: Within a largely zonal flow regime, a midlevel shortwave trough progressed eastward from the mid MS Valley to the OH Valley by the overnight of July 2nd. Accompanying this trough, a belt of 40-50 kt midlevel flow overspread areas along and south of the OH River, across KY/TN through this evening.  Likewise, a weak surface cyclone in northern IL will moved eastward to OH during the evening and overnight, while a trailing cold front moved slowly southeastward.  The cold front stalled just west of Kentucky, and zone of ascent preceding the midlevel trough supported scattered to numerous thunderstorms through the night, with the attendant threats of damaging winds and large hail.||In the wake of weakening morning convection across KY, boundary-layer dewpoints in the low-mid 70s spread northeastward from the Mid-South as surface heating in cloud breaks boosted MLCAPE into the 2500-3500 J/kg range with minimal convective inhibition.  Thunderstorm development began by early-mid afternoon along and ahead of the front across KY/TN and vicinity, and storms subsequently spread east-northeastward through late evening/early night.  The increasing mid-upper flow over the warm sector resulted in sufficiently long and relatively straight hodographs for supercells and organized clusters capable of producing damaging winds and large hail.  An isolated tornado or two was not ruled out by SPC, primarily where storms interact with lingering convective outflow/locally backed near-surface winds.  ||Two lines of thunderstorms rolled through eastern Kentucky throughout the afternoon and evening, each one resulting in widespread wind damage.
episodes.183551: A slow moving front and shortwave trough aloft approached from the west. Surface heating led to moderate instability and a severe thunderstorm was able to develop and produce damaging wind gusts and large hail as it moved through southeastern NY.
episodes.183557: A slow moving front and shortwave trough aloft approached from the west. Surface heating led to moderate instability and severe thunderstorms were able to develop and produce damaging wind gusts and large hail as they moved through southern CT.
episodes.183568: During the afternoon and evening hours of July 2nd, a broken line of showers and thunderstorms moved through Northwestern Kansas. Some of the storms became severe and produced hail up to pennies in size as well as damaging wind gusts. One storm in Gove County intensified and caused extreme straight-line wind damage. A NWS Storm Survey team was sent out and determined the maximum wind gusts to be up to 100 mph with this particular storm.
episodes.183603: A cluster of thunderstorms developed across eastern Minnesota and western Wisconsin. A few of the stronger storms produced some large hail and wind damage.
episodes.183604: A cluster of thunderstorms developed across eastern Minnesota and western Wisconsin. A few of the stronger storms produced some large hail and wind damage.
episodes.183619: A slow moving low pressure system produced an area of showers and embedded thunderstorms across eastern New York on July 2, 2023. One thunderstorm became severe during the evening hours downing numerous trees and an electrical wire in the Town of Hyde Park.
episodes.183668: Afternoon and early evening thunderstorms focused along a weak surface boundary from southwest Minnesota into areas south of Interstate 90 in southeast South Dakota.  Even with very weak deep-layer shear, modest surface-based instability of 1500-2000 J/kg led to the rapid development of storms, which peaked in mainly hail producing severity early in the life cycle, as well as an erratic tornado in eastern Bon Homme County.
episodes.183673: Evening thunderstorms focused along a weak surface boundary from northwest Iowa into areas south of Interstate 90 in southeast South Dakota. episodes.183682: Scattered thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the Rappahannock River.

episodes.183684: Scattered thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the Currituck Sound.

episodes.183933: A strong cold front and shortwave moved across Wyoming. Showers and thunderstorms mixed strong low level winds to the surface and brought numerous reports of wind gusts over 50 mph. The highest wind occurred in the Wind River Range where favored channeling brought wind gusts as high as 96 mph. In the lower elevations, the highest wind gust was 80 mph to the north of Casper. Wind gusts over 58 mph occurred in Fremont, Teton, Natrona, Sublette and Sweetwater Counties. In Fremont County, the wind capsized a kayak and threw two men into the water at Ocean Lake. One man could not be rescued and was presumed drowned. On the north shore of Lake Yellowstone, a microburst downed hundreds of trees in the Lake Village area of the park, blocking roads and causing a loss of power for multiple days.
episodes.183952: A cluster of thunderstorms moved into upstate South Carolina from northeast Georgia during the evening. A few of the embedded cells produced brief damaging wind gusts.
episodes.183955: For the third day in a row, scattered thunderstorms developed over the mountains and foothills during the afternoon and moved southeast. Once again, a few of the storms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts, mainly over the foothills.
episodes.183962: For the third day in a row, scattered thunderstorms developed near the North Carolina Blue Ridge and moved southeast into upstate South Carolina. Once again, a few of the storms produced damaging wind gusts and hail over the foothills.
episodes.184268: Scattered storms developed each afternoon hours and a few became strong to severe which downed some trees.
episodes.184531: A stationary front extended eastward from northeastern IN and far-northwestern OH, and across southern Lake Erie to the southern tier of Upstate New York during the evening of July 2nd. Simultaneously, a weak low drifted eastward along the front in northeastern IN. A line of multicell showers and thunderstorms evolved into a bow echo as the convection persisted eastward along the aforementioned front, moved onshore from south-central Lake Erie, and encountered moderate effective bulk shear and weak to moderate MUCAPE. The bow echo managed to produce sporadic straight-line convective wind damage in eastern Cuyahoga County.
episodes.184533: A stationary front extended eastward from northeastern IN and far-northwestern OH, and across southern Lake Erie to the southern tier of Upstate New York during the evening of July 2nd. Simultaneously, a weak low drifted eastward along the front in northeastern IN. A line of multicell showers and thunderstorms persisted eastward along the aforementioned front, encountered moderate effective bulk shear and weak to moderate MUCAPE, and generated a gale-force peak convective wind gust at the Cleveland Crib several miles offshore Lakewood.
episodes.184778: Scattered to widespread thunderstorms moved through the inland rivers, sounds, and coastal waters during the late afternoon and early evening bringing strong wind gusts.

A severe thunderstorm produced extreme damaging straight line winds estimated between 90 to 100 mph. Several large trees were snapped or uprooted with numerous small and large branches downed by the winds. One large branch landed on top of a metal outbuilding and punctured the roof. A few power poles were also broken or snapped with powerlines downed by the winds. Sprinklers were knocked over and an irrigation pivot was overturned over by the winds. A four inch by four inch wood post for a 4-way crossing sign was snapped by the winds causing the post and the sign to fall into a ditch to the southwest nearby. The damage path length was measured at 0.56 miles and the damage path width was measured at 0.94 miles. No injuries were reported. Wind speed estimates based on damage indicators.

A tornado spun up quickly at 1504 CST beneath a rapidly intensifying storm just north of 302nd Street in an open field between 425th and 426th Avenue. The tornado crawled through open country toward the north-northwest for several minutes and crossed Beaver Creek before damaging several trees on a farmstead along 425th Avenue. The tornado also ripped tin off an abandoned outbuilding. At this point, the tornado track veered to the north as it moved through soybean fields and across 301st Street before it lifted around a tenth of a mile north of 301st Street. The average path width for the tornado was 30 yards. The tornado was rated an EF-0 with a maximum estimated wind gust of 74 mph.

On Ocean Lake near Riverton WY, a kayak was capsized and two men were thrown into the water.
